So plcg causes consumption of PIP2. Also reaction where plcg is input and PIP2 is input or output (translocation). But the strongest is catalyst relation: plcg is catalyst, PIP2 is input. So cause plcg, effect PIP2? Hmm direction: catalyst acts on substrate; substrate is downstream? Usually enzyme acts on substrate, causing its conversion, so enzyme influence on substrate (consumption). That is a causal influence from enzyme to substrate modification. So we could state plcg causes change in PIP2 (hydrolysis). So cause=plcg, effect=PIP2. Confidence high due to multiple consistent reactions (multiple catalysts). No contradictory where PIP2 acts as catalyst on plcg. So confidence maybe 0.95.
